speakers.name: Sherry Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: MRC Expansion - CHIF Project Approval
said: Concerns about household hazardous waste program's efficiency and data.
Questions lack of detail on shredder location and mattress recycling funds.

description: Recommends new transit bylaw, requiring kenneled animals.

chips.text: Bus drivers face increased responsibility for unaccompanied children and dealing with incidents.
Councillor Dubois believed administration would review age limits across facilities
How will fines be collected from homeless individuals?
Mary Fedun reported daily unsafe situations, intoxication, and fare evasion on buses.
Sporadic enforcement risks charges of harassment and discrimination against certain groups.
Need for free tickets for citizens in least fortunate circumstances.
Administration will include app issue solutions in public communications and FAQs.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: New Saskatoon Transit Bylaw
said: Commends bylaw for bringing order; supports education and awareness.
Questions rules on sleeping, and age for accompanying children.
Calls for public engagement, fare review, and free tickets for vulnerable.

description: Committee recommends new tax abatements for market housing in established neighbourhoods.
It would repeal two existing housing incentive policies.

chips.text: Councillor Jeffries argued infill development is not meeting goals and needs incentives.
Developers would receive tax abatements for infill projects.
Definition of 'secondary corridors' remains undefined in policy.
Delegate Patrick Wolfe supported tax abatements for infill in older neighbourhoods.
Councillor Parker opposed market housing incentives in established neighbourhoods without zoning.
Top populations in core housing need: single mothers, seniors, Indigenous, new immigrants, refugees.
Administration will establish an affordable housing working group.

speakers.name: Patrick Wolfe
speakers.organization: concerns, stakeholders for a balanced approach to infill development
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Response to motions - New Development Incentives Policy
said: Supports tax abatements for infill in established older neighborhoods.
Infill development is expensive but financially benefits the city.
Incentives are crucial for building rental apartments in older areas.

description: Acquires land at 1130 and 1030 Idylwyld Drive North.
Purchases land from Saskatchewan government for $1.00.
Saskatoon would explore a strategic partnership with Muskeg Lake Cree Nation.

chips.text: City Manager stated an EOI would be disingenuous, likely leading to the same partner.
This direct negotiation approach for a project of this scale may set a new precedent.
The identity of other nations who approached the city for partnership was not disclosed.
One speaker expressed public distrust and concern over limiting the bidding process for the project.

speakers.name: Chief Kelly Wolfe
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: Muskeg Lake has a 38-year track record with urban reserves.
Partnership offers employment, tourism, and professional hockey opportunities.
Urban reserve status can unlock federal capital funding for the project.

speakers.name: Jason Aebig
said: Partnership with Muskeg Lake builds on a four-decade economic relationship.
Downtown district could inject $1.37 billion into the local economy.
Delay means higher costs and lost opportunities to host major events.

speakers.name: Cary Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: City's TIF financing plan for the district is broken.
Mayor Block may have already decided on this deal, excluding others.
Limiting bidding process to one partner destroys trust and competition.

speakers.name: Randy Pshebylo
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: Downtown and Riversdale districts are intricately connected; success benefits both.
First Nations have proven track records of economic leadership.
Supportive of continuing dialogue to find answers before dismissing anything.

speakers.name: Stephanie Pocha
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: Saskatoon's visitor economy reached nearly $900 million last year.
Supports exploring partnership with Muskeg Lake Cree Nation and STC chiefs.
Indigenous-led partnership offers a unique story no other city can tell.
